stories.headline: Xi opens a four-day party meeting focused on discipline
body: China's Communist Party leaders began a closed-door plenum on Monday to discuss tightening party discipline.
Xi Jinping delivered a work report on 'full and rigorous party self-governance'.
It comes about a year before Xi is expected to secure a fourth term as party leader.
stories.joke: The agenda: more discipline. The attendance: mandatory.
stories.vc: Policy signals from the plenum steer China's stimulus and tech rules, which ripple into global supply chains.

stories.headline: Trump's Justice Department brings a third case against James Comey
body: Sealed papers show the administration accuses the former FBI director of two counts of leaking national defence information.
Comey has not been indicted in this case and denies wrongdoing.
He called it political retribution and said he still believes in an independent judiciary.
stories.joke: Third time's the charm, says nobody in the legal profession.
stories.vc: Legal fights between the White House and its critics add to policy uncertainty that markets price into US assets.

stories.statLabel: of oil and LNG trade passed Hormuz
stories.headline: The Iran war is pushing up food costs across Africa
body: Trade officials warn that rising fuel and fertiliser prices from the Iran war threaten Africa's food security.
UNCTAD's Luz Maria de la Mora says many countries are using less fertiliser, which could cut next year's harvests.
Before the war, a fifth of global oil and LNG trade passed through the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.joke: Wars far away still send the bill to the dinner table.
stories.vc: Fertiliser and agritech startups that boost yields with fewer inputs suddenly have a much sharper sales pitch.

stories.headline: Jacinda Ardern joins the University of Sydney to teach leadership
body: New Zealand's former prime minister will lecture and mentor at the University of Sydney's school of public health.
Her work will focus on empathetic leadership, social cohesion and civic trust.
It is not a full-time teaching role; she will give guest lectures and masterclasses.
stories.joke: Office hours with a former PM. Attendance may exceed capacity.
stories.vc: Universities hiring big names is a bet on brand, the same playbook edtech platforms use with star instructors.

stories.headline: Australian court upholds a prison ban on Vegemite
body: A prisoner argued that banning Vegemite breached his human right to enjoy his culture as an Australian.
Justice Claire Harris agreed the ban limited his cultural rights but found it justified.
Prisons ban it to stop inmates using the yeast spread to brew alcohol.
stories.joke: Somewhere, a jar of Marmite is quietly relieved.
stories.vc: Proof that even a breakfast spread has a regulatory risk profile.

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli wins in Austin and closes in on the F1 title
body: The 20-year-old Mercedes driver won the US Grand Prix from pole, 13 seconds ahead of Charles Leclerc.
It was his ninth win of the season, stretching his lead over teammate George Russell to 123 points.
Antonelli can clinch the title in Mexico next week unless Russell wins there.
stories.joke: At 20, most of us were proud of passing our driving test.
stories.vc: A young superstar helps F1's US boom, which has turned team stakes into some of sport's hottest assets.

stories.headline: Tata Communications to spend up to $450M on fibre for AI
body: Tata Communications plans to invest about ₹4,350 crore to build 10,000 km of AI-ready fibre across India.
The network will link major data centres and AI hubs and connect to its global network.
It adds about 6 petabits per second of capacity, rolled out in phases from FY30 to FY36.
stories.joke: Your AI chatbot needs a faster road than your commute does.
stories.vc: Data centre buildout is creating demand for the 'plumbing' layer: fibre, cooling and power are investable themes in India.

stories.headline: Nazara swings back to profit as revenue jumps 52%
body: Nazara Technologies made a ₹35.4 crore profit in Q2, against a ₹33.9 crore loss a year earlier.
Operating revenue rose about 52% to ₹803.2 crore, helped by its BlueTile and BestPlay acquisitions.
Last year's loss included ₹914.7 crore in impairment charges.
stories.vc: Buying growth through acquisitions is working for now; investors will watch whether organic growth keeps pace.

stories.headline: Brain-game app Matiks raises $10M from General Catalyst
body: Indian puzzle and maths game app Matiks raised $10 million led by General Catalyst, with Ronnie Screwvala joining.
Daily users grew from 22,000 early this year to over 300,000 by September.
It had 2.2 million monthly users in September and has raised over $13.5 million in total.
stories.joke: Finally, screen time your maths teacher would approve of.
stories.vc: 'Anti-doomscroll' apps are a niche investors are warming to as feeds fill with AI content.

stories.headline: Pune Police ask Google and Apple to pull Rapido's app
body: Pune Police have written to Google and Apple asking them to remove Rapido over alleged unlicensed bike taxi services.
An FIR has been filed against its parent, Roppen Transportation Services.
Rapido's application for a bike taxi aggregator licence is still pending.
stories.joke: Two wheels, zero licences, one very annoyed RTO.
stories.vc: Bike taxi rules vary by state, and regulatory risk remains the biggest swing factor in Rapido's valuation.

stories.headline: Pronto's founder starts a physical AI data company in San Francisco
body: Pronto founder Anjali Sardana has launched Provision Labs to gather data for training and testing robots.
It will source data from professionals globally and work with developers building physical AI.
She stays CEO of Pronto, whose opt-in home recording pilot drew scrutiny.
stories.joke: From cleaning your home to teaching robots how to do it.
stories.vc: Real-world robot training data is scarce, so whoever collects it at scale becomes a picks-and-shovels play for physical AI.

stories.headline: Apple's new iPad mini gets an 8.5-inch OLED screen
body: The new iPad mini has a bigger 8.5-inch OLED display and Apple's A20 Pro chip.
It is 5.4 mm thin with peak brightness of 1,200 nits, more than double the last model.
It starts at $699 for Wi-Fi and $849 with cellular, days before Apple's Wednesday event.
stories.joke: Mini in name, OLED in spirit, maxi in price.
stories.vc: OLED spreading across Apple's line is a big win for display suppliers in Korea and China.

stories.headline: Fusion startups trade government shares for $260M in awards
body: Helion got $175 million and Commonwealth Fusion Systems $85 million from the US Commerce Department.
The money is for advanced chips used to power and control their reactors.
In return, both gave the government non-voting shares, a shift from the old no-strings grants.
stories.joke: Uncle Sam wants equity now. Next he'll want a board seat.
stories.vc: Government stakes dilute existing investors, changing the maths for deep-tech funds that relied on free grant money.

stories.headline: Turo will flag Teslas with Full Self-Driving to renters
body: Car-sharing platform Turo will show which Teslas on its marketplace have FSD (Supervised).
Eligible hosts get a free one-month FSD trial, verified through Tesla's API.
Tesla says about 1.7 million customers have paid for FSD out of over 10 million cars sold.
stories.joke: Rent the car, try the chauffeur, keep your hands on the wheel anyway.
stories.vc: Letting renters try FSD is a cheap way for Tesla to turn a one-off sale into a subscription habit.

stories.headline: Anthropic's filing shows how it keeps big customers hooked
body: More than half of customers spending $100,000+ now use both the Claude platform and an app like Claude Code or Cowork.
That's up from about 30% at the end of last year.
Anthropic counts 11,900 customers at $100k+, 1,900 at $1M+ and about 250 at $10M+.
stories.joke: Come for the API, stay for the apps, never leave.
stories.vc: Cross-product bundling is how Amazon and Uber built lock-in; investors will pay a premium if retention holds after IPO.
